lessonRef.focus: volume of cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: volume of cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

items.prompt: Mass 48 g, volume 6 cm³. Density and float?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A square patio of side 20 m is to be paved at $11 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $4400; the cost is proportional to the side length
$4400; the cost is proportional to the area
$880; the cost is proportional to the perimeter
$220; the cost is proportional to the area

items.prompt: Find the volume of a rectangular prism 9 by 6 by 9. Leave π in the answer where it appears.
Describe the cross-section formed by a sphere cut by any plane that meets it in more than one point.
A solid object has mass 48 g and volume 8 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
A square patio of side 10 m is to be paved at $24 per square metre. Find the total cost, and state which quantity the cost is proportional to.
choices: $960; the cost is proportional to the perimeter
$2400; the cost is proportional to the side length
$240; the cost is proportional to the area
$2400; the cost is proportional to the area

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a square pyramid with base edge 6 and height 10. Leave π in the answer where it appears.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Describe the cross-section formed by a cylinder cut by a plane perpendicular to its base through the axis.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A solid object has mass 72 g and volume 6 cm³. Find its density, and state whether it would float in water (density 1 g/cm³).
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
